description: Cluster Encrypted at Rest with an AWS Managed Key
rationale: MSK always encrypts the broker volumes, but a cluster created without a key of its own falls back on the AWS managed alias/aws/kafka key. That key has a policy the account cannot edit, so access to the data it protects cannot be narrowed, audited against a key policy, or revoked by disabling the key. It also cannot be shared, which means a snapshot or a copy of the data never leaves the boundary AWS chose for it. A customer managed key restores all of that, and its use is recorded in CloudTrail per calling principal.
remediation: Recreate the cluster with a customer managed KMS key for encryption at rest, as the key cannot be changed after creation, and restrict its key policy to the roles the cluster and its operators use
